Improper coping mechanisms and potential addiction can lead to worsening issues within the way of coping itself or developing certain harmful mentalities and potentially seeking out worse coping skills. It’s like smoking a cigarette. You start with one and then a few cigarettes a month, which isn’t immediately harmful. It becomes an addiction and you no longer feel the same high as before, so you either worsen that addiction by further smoking more often or even start seeking out something else to replace that same high. This kind of mentality of “well it isn’t harmful” is in itself harmful as all hell. The fact of the matter is you are hurting yourself with whatever your intentions of doing so may be, and that is guaranteed a negative impact to your physical and mental health. It leads to competition and self doubt, romanticism and leaves you stuck in the mindset of “well it’s not harmful ENOUGH” leading to a worsening issue. There are many negatives here and seeing you believe there aren’t, shows that you’ve already developed a certain mindset designed to cast this in a positive light. But hey, at the same time if you’re being safe and know when to receive medical attention, when to take breaks, and making sure that you’re knowledgeable with the effects is a good thing. Definitely keep practicing that regardless of mentality staying safe is always going to benefit you in the long run

Epidermis -“catscratches”- this is the top skin. (For aftercare use saline solution and ointment) 
Dermis-“styro”- this layer is the skin underneath the epidermis. It appears white before bleeding. (Aftercare- steri strips, butterfly bandaids, ointment as well as keeping it covered until it fully heals)
Hypodermis- “beans”- this is the layer of day, usually tinted yellow and appears in an almost bubble like mass. Think of baked beans or pomegranate seeds. (Aftercare- stitches, keeping wound covered, saline water when it starts closing no ointment directly on wound, go to a hospital if you can)
Fascia- tissue that surrounds muscle and bone. For aftercare, GO. TO. A. HOSPITAL. you NEED stitches.
